# Stay Different: Global Getaways in Ryokans, Villas, Gites & More


Imagine waking in a Japanese ryokan, a French farmhouse, or under the stars. With 89%* of travelers seeking experiences beyond standard hotels and 75**% looking to experience different ways of daily living, the demand for distinctive, immersive accommodations has never been higher. Booking.com explores trending property types*** around the globe, from rural gites to unique hostels, villas, and campsites; showcasing standout stay options that capture the essence of each destination.

A staple of rural travel in France, gites are self-catering stays dotted amongst the French countryside or located in smaller villages. With searches for gites up 20% amongst global travelers, these often-restored stone buildings or barns provide a more authentic connection to the local area and a taste of traditional French living. Gites originated from the French word "gesir" (to lie down) and trace their heritage to centuries of rural hospitality, when farmers, vintners and shepherds rented spare rooms or converted barns to passing travelers in areas without formal lodging.


Set in the Cassagnes countryside,


[Larroque Haute Gites](https://www.booking.com/hotel/fr/domaine-larroque-haute.html?) is a beautifully restored stone property that pairs traditional French character with bright, modern interiors. Original stone walls and exposed wooden beams celebrate the property's heritage, while stylish, modern living spaces provide every comfort. The two-bedroom property features a heated swimming pool, expansive gardens and peaceful outdoor seating areas, offering uninterrupted views across the surrounding woodland and rolling countryside. The broader Dordogne region is known for its vineyards, medieval towns and scenic walking routes, offering plenty of opportunities to explore beyond the property. Visitors to the region can dive into exploring the area on a


[canoe tour of the Dordogne Valley](https://www.booking.com/attractions/fr/prhdkbvwqdzb-dordogne-valley-canoe-tour.html) , moving through the gentle waters from Vitrac to take in the area’s natural beauty. Nearby villages host regular markets selling regional produce, while the surrounding Lot countryside is great for walking, cycling and vineyard visits.

Steeped in centuries of tradition, ryokans remain one of Japan’s most distinctive accommodation types with global searches for them on


[Booking.com](http://booking.com/) increasing by 9%. Ryokans, which date back to the 8th century,were resting places for Japan's nomads, are architecturally and philosophically centered around the onsen (natural hot spring) bathing ritual, with entire layouts designed around seasonal awareness and natural harmony. Combining hospitality, wellness and a deep connection to the surrounding nature, the inns usually incorporate tatami rooms, futon style beds and Japanese-style baths.


[Takaragawa Onsen Ousenkaku](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/takaragawa-onsen-ousenkaku.en-gb.html) ryokan is known for its expansive outdoor hot spring baths, which sit amid forests and natural scenery on the Takara river north of Minakami. Inside, simple yet elegant rooms reflect traditional Japanese design, with futon beds, low seating and tatami mat floors creating a calm retreat alongside the property's mineral-rich onsen baths. Traditional hospitality is woven throughout the stay, from yukata robes to seasonal meals showcasing ingredients from the surrounding mountain region. Against a backdrop of surrounding mountains and woodland, guests can soak while taking in views that are particularly striking in autumn, when the forests turn vibrant shades of red and gold, and in winter when snow blankets the landscape. A short journey from the property, visitors can explore Minakami's rivers and mountain trails, while nearby ski resorts and hiking routes make the area popular throughout the year.

Traditionally used to describe a country retreat, Villas offer travelers space, privacy and flexibility beyond a traditional hotel stay. Villas have become an increasingly popular accommodation choice for travelers looking to enjoy a destination on their own terms, with searches up 8%. From intimate 2-bedroom hideaways to expansive estates for large groups - with dedicated amenities like private pools, kitchens and outdoor entertaining spaces, there’s a villa to suit every type of trip


[Villa Tulia](https://www.booking.com/hotel/tz/villa-tulia-matemwe.html) is a beachfront retreat in


[Matemwe](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html) , a quiet-coastal village on the northeastern shore of Zanzibar’s main island Unguja. With space for up to eight guests, the villa is well suited to families and groups, with spacious indoor and outdoor living areas providing plenty of room for everyone to relax. Blending privacy with direct access to the island's natural beauty, the property showcases why villas are a popular choice for tropical vacations. Travelers can explore the coastline by boat, discover local villages or enjoy some of Zanzibar's most celebrated marine experiences including


[snorkeling in nearby Mnemba Atoll](https://www.booking.com/attractions/tz/prxwx0dcpuwk-snorkeling-at-mnemba-atoll.html) , known for its clear waters that are perfect for seeing vibrant coral reefs and marine life. Boat trips, reef snorkeling and visits to nearby fishing villages provide plenty to fill the days, before returning to meals prepared by a private chef overlooking white-sand beaches and turquoise waters.

Once the haunt of budget backpackers, hostels today often combine affordability with community and convenience, making them popular with travelers from all walks of life. The rise of “poshtels” means many now offer stylish, boutique feel rather than basic bunks and searches for hostels globally is up 40% YoY on Booking.com. Hostels lead with conversation-enabling design: open kitchens, communal dining tables, garden courtyards, co-working lounges and rooftop gathering spaces positioned as primary booking motivations rather than afterthoughts.


Located in the laid-back surf town of Puerto Escondido on the Pacific Coast of Oaxaca, Mexico,


[Puerto Dreams H](https://www.booking.com/hotel/mx/puerto-dreams-hostel.html) is known for its welcoming atmosphere, colorful communal spaces with vibrant murals and mix of private and shared rooms. Shared kitchens, co-working areas and organised activities including rooftop dance classes or group excursions allow guests to connect with the local wildlife while providing the perfect backdrop to meet fellow travelers. For a taste of local culture, visitors can join the


[Tequila and Mezcal Tasting](https://www.booking.com/attractions/mx/pr4muep9tqwr-mezcal-mole-and-chocolate-tasting.html) , learning about the heritage behind two of Mexico's best-known spirits while sampling regional flavours. Those looking to spend more time outdoors can also visit the nearby Hidden Port, on a


[Bioluminescent Night Tour](https://www.booking.com/attractions/mx/pr5wzutcbjl1-bioluminescent-night-tour.html) with the chance to witness the water glow after sunset in one of Puerto Escondido's most memorable natural experiences. This property makes the perfect resting place to come back to between surf lessons, beach hopping and evenings spent sampling mezcal with fellow travelers.

There's something truly magical about falling asleep under a canopy of stars. Searches for camping accommodation is up 6% YOY, appealing to travelers seeking an authentic and immersive connection to the outdoors. Today there’s a whole spectrum of camping style accommodations from traditional back-to-basics pre-pitched tents to "glamping"luxury yurts that bring together wilderness immersion with hotel-standard comfort.


[Zion View Camping](https://www.booking.com/hotel/us/zions-view-camping.html) on the Utah-Arizona border delivers on outdoor connection, without compromising on comfort. Here, travelers will experience panoramic views of stunning red rock landscapes, soaring mountains and endless desert scenery, coupled with spacious outdoor areas and communal gathering spaces that foster genuine connection. The property's peaceful setting makes it easy to switch off and soak up the natural surroundings, while its proximity to nearby attractions ensures there's plenty to discover beyond the grounds. Just a short drive from


[Zion National Park](https://www.booking.com/accommodation/region/us/zion-national-park.html) , the site is well placed for discovering the area's famous hiking trails, canyons and viewpoints. For those seeking a little more adventure, a


[UTV Slot Canyon Tour](https://www.booking.com/attractions/us/pru7riclcien-east-zion-experiences-utv-slot-canyon-tour.html) offers access to rugged desert landscapes and dramatic slot canyons beyond the national park.
